# espalier

`espalier` turns a tree of rule modules into per-directory documentation agents
read, and into a linter that enforces the same rules deterministically.

The documents under `docs/` are the specification. Where the code and a
document disagree, the document is right — so most of the rules here check that
the two still point at each other, rather than checking style.

## Structure

    ./
    ├─ docs/       the specification
    │
    ├─ ignores/    the ignore lists espalier ships
    │
    ├─ src/        the implementation
    │
    ├─ test/       the argument that the tool works
    │
    ├─ HANDOFF.MD  the record of what was decided and why (required)
    │
    └─ README.MD   the front page (required)

Nothing else may exist under this directory.

## HANDOFF.MD — the record of what was decided and why

Every decision that cost an argument is written down here,
struck through rather than deleted when it is superseded. A reversal that
leaves no trace is a decision that will be made again.

## README.MD — the front page

Opens with a level-one heading, and links into `docs/` for
anything it only summarizes. The front page is allowed to be shorter than the
specification; it is not allowed to be a second, drifting copy of it.

## Not described here

### Exclusion rules

Rules appear in evaluation order. A leading `!` retains a path that an earlier rule excluded.

| Rules | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `LEGACY_README.MD`<br>`node_modules/`<br>`dist/` | — |
| `.cache/` | — |
| `.git/`<br>`.hg/`<br>`.svn/` | Version control metadata. `.gitignore` never lists `.git/` — git has no need to ignore itself — so this is the one exclusion no other file supplies. |
| `.gitignore`<br>`.gitattributes`<br>`.gitmodules`<br>`.mailmap`<br>`.git-blame-ignore-revs`<br>`.editorconfig`<br>`.dockerignore`<br>`.tool-versions` | Repository metadata. Tracked on purpose, and dictated by the tool that reads them rather than by this project's architecture. |
| `.github/`<br>`.gitlab/`<br>`.gitlab-ci.yml`<br>`.circleci/`<br>`.buildkite/`<br>`.travis.yml`<br>`azure-pipelines.yml`<br>`Jenkinsfile`<br>`.drone.yml`<br>`.woodpecker.yml` | Continuous integration. |
| `LICENSE`<br>`LICENSE.*`<br>`LICENCE`<br>`LICENCE.*`<br>`COPYING`<br>`NOTICE`<br>`AUTHORS`<br>`CONTRIBUTORS` | Licence and legal. |
| `.vscode/`<br>`.idea/`<br>`.fleet/`<br>`.zed/`<br>`.claude/`<br>`.cursor/`<br>`.windsurf/`<br>`.continue/`<br>`.codeium/`<br>`.aider*`<br>`*.swp`<br>`.DS_Store`<br>`Thumbs.db`<br>`desktop.ini` | Editor and operating system droppings. |
| `package.json`<br>`package-lock.json`<br>`npm-shrinkwrap.json`<br>`yarn.lock`<br>`pnpm-lock.yaml`<br>`pnpm-workspace.yaml`<br>`bun.lock`<br>`bun.lockb`<br>`deno.json`<br>`deno.jsonc`<br>`deno.lock` | Manifests and lockfiles. |
| `tsconfig.json`<br>`tsconfig.*.json`<br>`jsconfig.json`<br>`.eslintrc`<br>`.eslintrc.*`<br>`eslint.config.*`<br>`.prettierrc`<br>`.prettierrc.*`<br>`prettier.config.*`<br>`.babelrc`<br>`.babelrc.*`<br>`babel.config.*`<br>`.npmrc`<br>`.nvmrc`<br>`.node-version` | Tool configuration. The tool decides the filename; the project only decides the contents. |
| `fixtures/**` | espalier's own fixtures are data: sixty configs, several deliberately invalid, and a root run executing all sixty is not what anyone means by it. |
| `LEGACY_README.MD` | Not source, and not in .gitignore either. |

### Tool-owned entries

| Entries | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `.espalierignore`, `.gitignore`, `espalier`, `espalier.config.yaml` | Configuration. Read by `espalier`, not by this project. |
| `AGENTS.MD` | Generated by `espalier build`; edits here will be overwritten. Modify [`ESPALIER.MD`](espalier/ESPALIER.MD) to change this document's persistent guidance. |

Nothing above describes these as project structure. They are not alternative destinations for work that does not fit the structure above.

## Checking your work

Run `espalier lint` before you finish. Every violation it reports arrives with
the rule text attached, so a failure tells you what to do and not only what is
wrong.

## Amending this structure

This file is generated from `espalier/`, and the structure it describes is not
yours to change. If the work does not fit — a file has nowhere legal to go, or a
rule is wrong for the task — YOU MUST stop and report the gap. YOU MUST NOT
widen a pattern, add a rule, or edit `espalier/` to make an error go away.
Deciding the shape of this project is the architect's job, and a task that
appears to require changing that shape is a task to hand back, not to unblock.
